key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn explicit corrections to a simple k-ε-b turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor transition predictions while keeping the model interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to retrofit low-order RANS models for transitional mixing problems where standard closures miss key physics but full DNS is too expensive.
method: Embed the k-ε-b model inside a surrogate PINN.
Calibrate closure coefficients and learn corrective terms for missing physics.
Re-express the learned corrections as analytical modifications using state variables and flow indicators.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is evaluated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and is reported to improve mixing-layer growth predictions during the transition to turbulence.
watch_item: The learned closure is tailored to a specific transitional regime, so transferability to other buoyancy-driven flows or higher-Re turbulence should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
